component: execution model D042 + D079 + D106, live process lifecycle
rule: D042 condition 1; D079 items 1-2; D106 (Q15); D034 rationale
summary: D042 condition 1 says the protective SL always resides on the exchange so a VPS outage never leaves a position unprotected. Since D079 the entry is a GTD LIMIT with no stop until the process sees a fill. A crash, reboot or network partition while an entry rests leaves an order that can fill with nothing to place its stop; the live service has restart "no". The risk was named a Phase 24 blocker in 20-DEFERRED and then dropped; the Demo-accepted alternative (pre-placed reduceOnly stop) and the outage risk were never compared for the owner.
expected: Either no position can exist without an exchange-resident stop when the host dies, or the residual risk is stated in numbers and accepted by the owner in a DECISIONS row.
actual: The two decisions contradict each other. No exchange-side dead-man switch exists (no countdownCancelAll use in src). Cancel-on-stop (24-DEFERRED R-22, Phase 25) covers a requested stop only. The blocker row of 20-DEFERRED line 134 does not appear in the Phase 24 or 25 planning files.
impact: Mainnet: one outage while an entry rests can lose up to the isolated margin, about 88 USDT at equity 1000 (planned risk 5 USDT, daily stop 10 USDT), roughly 17R. Daily stop, caps and SAFE_MODE do not act because the process is down. ISOLATED margin is the only bound.
evidence: DECISIONS D042: "(1) the protective SL always resides on the exchange so a VPS outage never leaves a position unprotected". D079: stop "placed after the first fill with positive quantity". RUNBOOK.md:1182: "The process does not cancel resting entries on stop, so a GTD LIMIT entry that is still resting can fill while the process is down or restarting and stay without a stop until the next start protects it." docker-compose.yml:232 restart: "no". 20-DEFERRED.md:134 "VPS or process down while an entry rests ... [DOC], [NOT_TESTED]". 19-NOTES.md:16 "Model (b) ... the Demo showed it accepted and sized equal to the position [DEMO], but it is not built". grep -ri countdownCancel src: no match.
reproduction: Arithmetic: tmp/decisions_trading_soundness/viability.py (column naked_max_loss_R: 8-21R depending on the stop distance).
why_tests_miss: Every test starts from a running coordinator; Demo smokes are attended runs from the development machine (host behaviour NOT_OBSERVED per D106).
recommendation: Owner chooses: probe and arm countdownCancelAll while an entry rests; or build the pre-placed reduce-only stop; or accept in writing with restart unless-stopped and a short entry lifetime. Amend D042 condition 1 either way.
known_prior: KNOWN:20-DEFERRED 'Blockers carried to Phase 24' (dropped afterwards); KNOWN:24-DEFERRED R-22 (graceful stop only); 2026-09-29 audit docs_trading_soundness recommended a dead-man auto-cancel

component: research run 1, kill gate D013, Phase 26 goal
summary: The pooled Validation mean net R of all 48 registered candidates is printed in committed evidence: 45 are negative, the best three are +0.0027, +0.0007 and +0.0137 R (best naive z +0.09). No candidate of any of the three families can pass G2 (lower 95 % bound above 0) or G3 (Holm over 48). The executable gate was deferred to Phase 26 while Phases 17-24 were built.

impact: The owner steers the project without the fact that decides whether the execution half is needed. No paper or Demo result of a01 can support a go. This is the protocol's own outcome, not an opinion on profitability.

component: RESEARCH_PROTOCOL v2.6.0 section 4 (G3, G5), amendment procedure
summary: The family-wise bound of G3 covers the 48 hypotheses of run 1 only; a new protocol version starts a new set with a fresh alpha on Validation data whose outcome is now visible in committed evidence. G5 (holdout) requires only mean above 0 and 30 trades, which a zero-edge candidate passes about half the time. Amendments v2.5.0 and v2.6.0 were made after Validation performance figures were printed (2026-10-16).
expected: A rule for the error rate across successive runs on the same data and a holdout test that a zero-edge candidate usually fails.
actual: No cross-run rule; G5 has no interval or p-value; performance figures are printed in 'reporting only' sections before any gate is evaluated.
impact: After the failed run 1 the protocol becomes permissive exactly when a second run is likely: P(false Validation pass) = 1 - 0.95^k over k runs, times about 0.5 for G5. The two late amendments changed no threshold and the rerun stayed negative, so no false pass came from them.
evidence: Protocol G3: "over ONE set of 48 candidate-level p-values ... never extended by a re-run"; G5: "passes only when mean net R after full costs is above 0 and maximum drawdown is at most 20%". git log: 16-46-run-output.txt committed 2026-10-16 08:23 +0700 with mean_r lines; D073 and D075 dated 2026-10-17.
recommendation: Before any run 2 the owner decides alpha spending across runs, a fresh Validation period (data after 2026-10-03) and a lower-bound condition for G5; stop printing performance figures before the gate is evaluated.

summary: Once a stop was confirmed and seen by id, one by-id answer 'not found' or 'not active' is final: with an open position the plan goes to CLOSE_REQUIRED, the position is closed at market and SAFE_MODE is entered; the listing cross-check is skipped on purpose. The same query is recorded on Demo as answering 'not found' for a resting stop (2026-10-22, 2026-11-01, 2026-11-15). D113 added rereads to the take-profit step only. A flat conclusion needs two reads; a lost stop needs one.
expected: An irreversible, money-moving action rests on more than one read of an endpoint with a recorded false-negative history.
actual: Single read in _supervise_stop on every protection step for the life of the position.
impact: A transient false negative closes a healthy protected position at market (about 0.15R of costs at the ceiling plus the forfeited trade) and blocks entries until a manual SAFE_MODE exit. Fail-safe, not unsafe.
evidence: protection.py:2372-2373 "if tracked.stop_confirmed_at is not None and tracked.stop_by_id_seen: return answer"; :2333-2336 "if reading in (_StopReading.ABSENT, _StopReading.NOT_ACTIVE): await self._on_stop_lost(tracked)"; D113: "Binance Demo answered the query by client id with not found for a stop that rested, as it did on 2026-10-22 (plan 20-27) and for TAKE_PROFIT_2 on 2026-11-01" (leading explanation, not proven).
reproduction: Not run; code trace PROTECTED -> _supervise_stop -> ABSENT -> _on_stop_lost -> _position_is_open True -> _enter_close_required(B4).
why_tests_miss: Fakes answer consistently; no fake models a false negative on a resting stop.
recommendation: Owner decision: keep D077 as is and accept the cost, or require a second witness (listing or N consecutive negatives) before B4; measure the false-negative rate in the Phase 25 campaign.
known_prior: KNOWN:20-DEFERRED 'Stop-out looks like a lost stop (D077)' covers a mid-trigger stop only; KNOWN:D113 covers the take-profit step only

component: sizing and quantization at 500-1000 USDT; D040 canary
rule: owner goal (capital 500-1000 USDT); D035; D040; D046
summary: At 0.5 % risk 1R is 2.5-5 USDT. ETH, BNB, SOL and XRP size cleanly (utilisation 93-100 %). BTC with step 0.001 is accepted at equity 500 only for stops under about 2.4 % and is rejected at BTC 120,000 with a 1 % stop; the 50-100 USDT canary of D040 can never trade BTC. Round-trip costs are 15 % of 1R at the tightest allowed stop. A real edge of +0.10R on 250 trades a year would be 62-125 USDT a year, below plausible hosting costs (assumed, not from the repo).

summary: The last-price age bound was raised from 5 s to 30 s because the quiet Demo book made 5 s refuse normal moments. The value is shared with LIVE on the unmeasured assertion that a mainnet book changes every second.
